title: Chapter 39: An All-Nighter Pledge
content:
Chapter 39:

A Late-Night Promise

Accompanied by Rem, who was fully combat-ready with her “self-defense” iron ball in one hand, the search of the forest at night continued.

Blocked by the trees, the moonlight failed to reach the ground, leaving the forest steeped in deep, jet-black darkness. As he dodged the trees that stood in his path and pushed through the underbrush, he accumulated bloody scratches all over his body.

The stinging pain of the small cuts, combined with the irritation of groping blindly through the dark.

Coupled with the lack of time, these factors weighed heavily on Subaru’s mind.

“Honestly, I didn’t expect it to be 

this

 dark. You’re holding up surprisingly well, Rem-rin.”

“Rem has a divine protection when in forests or mountains… More importantly, please keep your voice down. Control your breathing, too. Your heartbeat is loud.”

“Like… I… could…”

Retorting in a whisper, punctuating every syllable, he slowly followed behind Rem.

Without her, he would have lost track of where he was and been stranded by now. Whether she had night vision or not, Rem’s steps were light and unhesitating.

She was blazing a trail through the forest darkness—which Subaru couldn’t even vaguely see through—making it easier for him to follow.

At the bottom of this darkness where even moonlight felt distant, the only thing he could rely on was Rem’s back ahead of him. Her small frame looked so large in his eyes that he instinctively reached out and pinched the hem of her maid outfit.

“…What are you doing?”

“‘A man who involuntarily ends up clinging due to the loneliness of the dark’—scene.”

“If you’re holding on so you don’t get separated, please hold my shoulder properly.”

“I didn’t want to get in the way of your confident stride. But I couldn’t handle the anxiety. My fragile maiden heart just couldn’t help itself…”

“The nerve… and you were actually a little cool earlier, too.”

Rem looked utterly exasperated. Allowing him to keep holding her hem, she stopped, looked around the area, and sniffed the air lightly.

Pointing at her police-dog-like behavior,

“You’ve been doing that a lot. Can you actually track things by smell?”

“It is the one thing that cannot be deceived. Appearance and voice can be faked, but the scent that exudes from one’s very existence cannot.”

Rem’s assertion was brimming with confidence. Because of that, he could only pray that her sense of smell would lead them to their target.

Suddenly, watching her, he felt like he’d had a conversation with Rem based on scent before. That time, yes, the ‘Witch’s Scent’ had been the issue. Rem had said that Subaru gave off a loathsome stench.

Thinking back, he remembered Beatrice mentioning something similar about him. The situation didn’t allow for it now, but if things were resolved and he still remembered—

“—! Nearby. It’s the smell of a living creature.”

Beside the deep-in-thought Subaru, Rem turned her face to the right and narrowed her eyes. Subaru followed her gaze, but all he saw was the same unchanging darkness.

Feeling frustrated by his limitations, he turned back to Rem.

“Is it the scent of the kids?!”

“It cannot be said for sure, but it does not smell like a beast.”

“That’s good enough for me. Let’s go!”

“This way.”

Rem lowered her posture and took off, and Subaru scrambled after her, still clutching the hem of her dress.

He fancied there was a brighter ring to Rem’s voice. Having found a literal ray of light in the darkness, his feet moved faster without him even thinking about it.

However, hope and anxiety were two sides of the same coin.

The fact that Rem hadn’t asserted the scent belonged to the children was likely because, subconsciously, she recognized that anxiety as well.

That was precisely why the two of them needed to find the answer as quickly as possible.

Rem, taking the lead, swung her iron ball violently, gouging out trees that spanned the width of the path to clear a way. Her rough handling of the obstacle betrayed her intense impatience, and naturally, Subaru found himself pushing off the ground harder as he chased after her.

His breath ran short, his legs grew heavy. Yet, his mind was clear. His eyes gradually began to adjust to the pitch blackness, and the scenery of the forest started to faintly register in Subaru’s vision.

Suddenly, Subaru’s field of vision opened up. There was a clearing in the forest where the trees parted like a gaping mouth. A small hill rose there, open to the sky, and the moonlight pouring down created an atmosphere that was almost fantastical.

On that small green hill, in that place bathed in the brilliant blessing of moonlight—

“It’s the kids!”

Lying limp on the green carpet of grass were the children, their limbs sprawled out.

He rushed over in a panic, checking their condition alongside Rem.

There were six of them lying there in total. There were no visible external wounds on their skin, and while all of them were unconscious, they were still breathing.

“They’re alive. —They’re alive!”

We made it!

 Subaru cheered, clenching his fist.

But beside him, Rem, who was examining the condition of a sleeping girl, prefaced with a “No,” and said,

“They are breathing for now, but their debilitation is too severe. At this rate…”

“Debilitation… The curse!”

Looking closely, the children’s faces were ghastly pale, gasping for breath like fish out of water. Cold sweat beaded on their foreheads, and their sleeping expressions were pained, as if they were being tormented by nightmares.

Curse arts—seeing from an external view the very thing that also had attacked his body time and again, Subaru bit his lip.

“Can’t we do something? Anything? Can you break the curse, Rem?”

“With Rem’s skill, it is impossible… If only Sister were watching this place right now.”

Just like Subaru, driven by frustration, Rem admitted her own lack of power with regret. However, she immediately shook her head as if to shake off that weakness.

“In any case, Rem will cast healing magic, even if it is only a temporary comfort. We need to restore their strength, even a little.”

“Yeah, please. What should I do?”

“Keep watch over the surroundings. And please gather the children in one spot.”

Following Rem’s instructions, he lined the children up before her. Looking pained at the sight of the children breathing so laboriously, Rem used the handle of her flail to carve a circle into the ground.

It was a circle that completely encompassed the children. She crouched at the edge and touched it.

“Healing of water, grant us your blessing—”

Following the chant, a pale blue light rose from within the crude circle, softly covering the bodies of the sleeping children before slowly soaking into them.

It was a gentle, soft glimmer—one that even Subaru, with his poor knowledge of magic, could feel was a wave of healing.

As time passed, the light permeated the children’s bodies, and their pained breathing gradually began to ease, if only slightly.

“That’s amazing, Rem. With this…”

“Rem told you, it is only a temporary comfort. They may be fine while Rem can speak to the mana within their bodies like this, but once that is depleted, this won’t even serve as first aid. We must eliminate the root cause immediately.”

“Breaking the curse, right. We have no choice but to go back to the mansion and rely on Beako and Puck. Alright, let’s head back. We’ll carry the kids and…”

“—Subaru?”

Just as he steeled himself for an immediate retreat, Subaru was startled to hear his name called. Turning toward the voice, he saw a brown-haired boy with his eyes slightly open.

The boy, who seemed to have regained consciousness, reflected Subaru in his eyes and gasped painfully,

“Subaru, Suba…”

“You awake, Lucas? Good, that’s a good boy, strong boy. But don’t push yourself. I’ll get you home right away and say goodbye to whatever’s hurting you. Just leave it to me, rest quietly for now and…”

“One… deeper in… still… deeper.”

“…Hey, what did you say?”

Lucas was trying to convey something in broken gasps.

Sensing something he couldn’t ignore in that fragmented information, Subaru asked again. But his voice did not reach Lucas, who had closed his eyes and lost consciousness once more.

Subaru muttered a quiet “damn it,” then turned his gaze toward the depths of the forest.

“If the missing brats are the crew that was at that spot this afternoon… Ah, dammit, seriously? I don’t see that girl with the braids.”

There were six sleeping here, all children whose names he knew. But the one missing was the girl who had led Subaru to the puppy earlier that day. The shy, timid kid who had trouble joining their circle.

She was nowhere to be found. And in his brief moment of consciousness, Lucas hadn’t said “help me” or “it hurts”—he had said “she was taken deeper in.”

A child not even ten years old, while in a life-threatening situation himself, had worried about the safety of a friend over his own.

“Goddammit.”

Cursing one more time, Subaru stood up.

Rem, who perhaps hadn’t heard the exchange with Lucas clearly, looked puzzled. Subaru turned to her, pointed a finger, and asked,

“Question, Rem. If you keep casting healing magic on the children, can you extend the time limit?”

“…In the current situation, yes, it is possible. But truly, that will only serve to buy time. And Rem will be completely tied down here.”

Unable to read Subaru’s intent, Rem’s response was hesitant.

As he listened, Subaru’s brain spun at high speed. What should he do? What was the best move for his useless self to make in this situation?

There was only one option he could think of. It would be a massive gamble, but—

“Rem. One of the kids has been taken further in. I think that’s where this ‘witchbeast’ is.”

“Further in… but if she were taken singly, then that…”

He stopped Rem from voicing her worst-case scenario with an outstretched palm. Silencing her, Subaru furrowed his brow.

“I know the situation is bad. But we managed to save the lives of these kids when I thought it was hopeless. So we should make the effort to save the last one too, right?”

“If you get greedy, you might end up dropping what you could have successfully brought back.”

“That’s exactly why you’re here, isn’t it, Rem? To make sure that doesn’t happen.”

Rem looked taken aback as she tried to object. Subaru spread his arms wide in front of her.

“With your strength, Rem, carrying six kids and running isn’t impossible, right? On the flip side, I like to think I’m pretty strong, but carrying six brats is impossible for me. At best two, maybe three if I push it. I can’t use healing magic, so right now, there’s basically nothing I can do here. So, we should make effective use of the free piece on the board.”

“…”

“I’ll go check deeper in. Rem, you take the kids and head back to the village for now. —Look, I’m not gonna do anything impossible, rash, or reckless—I couldn’t even if I wanted to. Once you hand the kids over to the villagers, you just need to fly back here.”

Rem listened silently to Subaru’s absurd logic.

Feeling that her gaze wasn’t softening in the slightest, Subaru continued to rattle on, using every bit of his glib tongue.

“The kid further in… well, if it’s the worst-case scenario, I’ll turn back too. But if there’s still hope, I can at least buy some time.”

“We don’t know what kind of enemy we’re dealing with, and we don’t know how long it will take for Rem to return. Worst case, Rem might lose track of you and be unable to rejoin…”

Finding Subaru’s decision hard to accept, Rem grabbed his sleeve and argued more fervently.

Was she worried about him? Or could she simply not stomach such a reckless plan?

Thinking it would be nice if it were the former, Subaru gave a wry smile and pried her fingers from his sleeve. Then, taking her now-free fingers in his hand,

“Oh, you won’t lose track of me.”

“On what grounds…”

“Oh, I’ve got grounds alright.”

Laughing, Subaru touched his own nose with his finger, then pointed it at her face.

“Your nose, you’re confident in it, right? And turns out, I actually give off a pretty pungent smell—I’ve had it pointed out to me a few times by a certain Rem-rin and Beako.”

Rem fell silent, her eyes widening.

He pointed double fingers at her shocked face, as if getting revenge on the Rem from another time—the her that this Rem didn’t know.

“Even if nobody else notices, 

you

 will notice my smell. The stench clinging to me, the lingering scent of a sinner—isn’t that right?”

“Subaru… just how much do you know…?”

“Who knows? I’m clueless about most things. I don’t know anything, and no matter how many times I repeat yesterday, today, and tomorrow, I just can’t seem to reach the answer I want.”

Rem looked bewitched by the sudden leap in conversation. While he thought her reaction was unavoidable, he was also somewhat amazed at his own state of mind, being able to turn this into a laughing matter.

He wanted to pat himself on the back for developing such nerves of steel.

“Just like you have a mountain of things you want to ask me, I’ve got a mountain of things I want to ask you. So, let’s talk once this is all over. We’ll do it all night in one of our rooms, in our pajamas—a late-night girl talk. It’s a promise, yeah?”

Saying that, he forcibly entwined his finger with hers, which he still had been holding.

With their pinkies linked, Rem looked at Subaru with bewildered eyes. In front of her, Subaru shook their linked fingers up and down in a big motion.

“There, pinky sworn!”

“Wh-What was that…?”

“It’s a ritual for making promises in my hometown. If you break it, you have to swallow a thousand needles. Since it’s a thousand hits of one damage each, it’s an instant kill move in an RPG where you only have three-digit HP.”

Barraged by this, Subaru’s behavior was now beyond Rem’s comprehension. To Rem, who was speechless with layer upon layer of confusion, Subaru prefaced with, “In short,”

“I trust you, Rem-rin. So, I want to act in a way that makes you trust me, too. Let’s make a promise for that right now.”

“————”

“I told you, didn’t I? I’m the type who keeps promises and makes others keep them. So, you don’t need to worry about me—I’m totally hunky-dory.”

“‘Hunky-dory’…”

Finally unable to hold back, Rem let out an exasperated sigh and laughed weakly.

Unable to fully suppress the urge, Rem continued to chuckle softly, and as if infected by it, Subaru also laughed while keeping his voice down.

After laughing for a moment and finishing, Rem looked up and said,

“We have made a promise. —Rem really will be asking you to tell me all sorts of things, you know.”

“I’ll tell you anything, even the name of my first crush. Anything except the name of the girl I’m currently in love with.”

“Rem already knows that one.”

“Even though it never seems to get through to her!”

An exchange that felt like something he had left behind somewhere.

By recreating it, Subaru found his own satisfaction. Rem, too, with a serious expression,

“Rem will return immediately. Please, never do anything reckless. Or Lady Emilia will get angry.”

“I don’t want Emilia-tan getting mad at me either, so I’ll be careful. —Well, besides, I’ll be fine. I’m pretty demonically possessed today.”

“Demonically, possessed…?”

“It’s the demon version of being divinely possessed! Lately it’s been my favorite!”

Crossing his arms and spreading his legs, he struck a new pose, grasping at the empty air.

What did Rem think of Subaru’s frivolous bluff, he wondered.

She didn’t comment on his attitude,

“See you later.”

Leaving those words behind, she scooped up the children all at once. The sight of a petite girl carrying six people—even if they were children—on her small shoulders looked like something out of a street performance. Even in a situation like this, Subaru couldn’t help but laugh as he watched her back recede.

Left all alone on the small hill in the forest, Subaru exhaled deeply in the world upon which silence had fallen. Slowly, he turned toward the direction in question.

“Well then, time to get to work, Subaru.”

He said it as if to rouse his trembling self. Biting down hard on the pinky finger that had sworn the promise, he broke into a run.

—Waiting at his destination: was it despair, hope, or something else entirely?

The morning of the fourth day, which he should have reached time and again, now felt so far away.
